claims.text: The component material's physical and microstructural characteristics cause hot cracking during traditional fusion-welding repair.
Mechanically alloyed CrFeNiMo, Co0.5CrFeNiMo, and Al0.5CrFeNiMo powders sieved to 80 µm or less are applicable to ESD repair on a C1018 steel substrate.
The proposed SPS temperatures are 1050 °C for CrFeNiMo, 1000 °C for Co0.5CrFeNiMo, and 950 °C for Al0.5CrFeNiMo.
SPS at the proposed temperatures produces low-porosity, diffusely alloyed, machinable HEA electrodes.
The repair coating is deposited by ESD in either three or six layers.
The specified SPS process uses 50 MPa pressure, a 50 °C/min heating rate, a 5 min dwell, and a 30 °C/min cooling rate in graphite tooling.
The specified ESD process uses a 5 L/min argon shield and, for CrFeNiMo, pulse settings of 30 µF, 100 V, and 360 Hz.
Increasing SPS temperature promotes particle diffusion and homogenization in the HEA electrode.
Increasing SPS temperature promotes pore closure and densification in the HEA electrode.
The proposed SPS treatment produces a refined, multiphase HEA electrode microstructure.
Successive ESD layers fill voids and improve coating continuity.
Excessive ESD layering may increase oxidation or superficial microcracking.
ESD locally remelts and mixes the deposited HEA material with the substrate.
ESD avoids the extended high-temperature exposure associated with full fusion-welding repair.
Rapid, localized ESD reduces thermal stresses relative to full fusion-welding repair.
Reduced thermal exposure and thermal stress lower the risk of repair-induced hot cracking.
Coatings made with the higher-temperature SPS electrodes will be denser and less porous than coatings or specimens made with the lower-temperature SPS conditions.
Coatings made with the higher-temperature SPS electrodes will have greater hardness than lower-temperature SPS specimens and traditional fusion-weld repairs.
A six-layer ESD coating will provide greater repair coverage than a three-layer coating.
The ESD repair will enable reliable service under aggressive conditions with less hot cracking and better structural integrity than traditional fusion-weld repair.
